questions.question:

= 48 - 24 = 24 and 48 - 36 = 12

questions.question: If it was a Monday on 1 January 2018, what was the day of the week on 31 December 2018?
questions.solution:
1 January 2018 to 1 January 2019 = 365 days i.e. 52 weeks and 1 odd day i.e. Tuesday.

So the day before one day of 1 January 2019 is 31 December 2018 is Monday.

Hence, the correct answer is Monday.

questions.question:
Three of the following four numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different.

Pick the number that is different from the rest.

Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two

numbers of the following number-pair.

6 : 40
questions.solution:
Given series

6 : 40

The pattern followed here is,

(First term)² + 4 = Second term

= 6² = 36; 36 + 4 = 40

Option 1:

15 : 45

= 15² = 225; 225 + 4 = 229 ≠ 45

Option 2:

5 : 25

= 5² = 25; 25 + 4 = 29 ≠ 25

Option 3:

**7 : 53 **

**= 7² = 49; 49 + 4 = 53**

Option 4:

9 : 72

= 9² = 81; 81 + 4 = 85 ≠ 72

Hence, the correct answer is 7 : 53.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-pair in the same way as the second letter-pair is related to the first letter-pair.

DH : HL : : GK : ?
questions.solution:
According to the alphabetical positions of the letters,

DH = D + 4 = H 

HL = H + 4 = L

Similarly,

GK = G + 4 = K

K + 4 = O

Hence, the correct answer is KO.

questions.question: If BUS is coded as 126 and FUEL is coded as 176, then how will SHRUB be coded as?
questions.solution:
According to the alphabetical positions of the letters,

The code for BUS = 2 + 21 + 19 = 42; 42 × 3 = 126 (as 3 letters are present)

FUEL = 6 + 21 + 5 + 12 = 44; 44 × 4 = 176 (as 4 letters are present)

Similarly, the code for

SHRUB = 19 + 8 + 18 + 21 + 2 = 68; 68 × 5 = 340 (as 5 letters are present)

Hence, the correct answer is 340.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All hens are eggs.

All eggs are birds.

Some eggs are lions.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some lions are eggs.

II. Some eggs are hens.

III. Some eggs are birds.

options.text: Either conclusion II or III follows.
Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97c2f1b45500eea8f2cb3b39803a8673053be14a67aa8cba963c8176e262cb4e.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some lions are eggs → True (as per diagram, some lions is eggs)

II. Some eggs are hens → True (as per diagram, some eggs are hens)

III. Some eggs are birds → True (as per diagram, some eggs are birds)

Hence, all the conclusions follow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

Some is a subset of all.

If it is given that, 'All A are B' then the conclusion 'Some A are B' will always follow.
